Khodoriv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. A Jewish community here dates at least to 1642, when a wooden synagogue was established, and grew alongside the town's economy after a railway was built through it, reaching roughly half the population by 1890. Nazi forces occupied Khodoriv in July 1941; by September 1942 some 2,000 Jews had been deported to the Belzec extermination camp, and most of the roughly 400 spared for forced labor were killed the following February. The cemetery itself was destroyed after the war when a stadium was built on the site in the 1990s — locals say surviving gravestones were relocated by the Jewish community beforehand, though the ESJF has not been able to locate them.
